A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Search Self-play work. All 33 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: v2 reports original SSP evaluations on seven QA benchmarks, alongside ablations and training-dynamics results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark evaluations, ablations and training-dynamics results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1 and Appendix D retain the same proposer–solver procedure, RAG filtering, optimization objectives and prompts. The newly named default RAG verifier is an implementation disclosure; the PDFs do not establish a procedural change between versions.

E1.justification: Evaluation still covers NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue and Bamboogle. The training-answer sources in Appendix A.4 and the Wiki-2018 retrieval environment are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Qwen2.5, LLaMA-3.1, Qwen3, ZeroSearch, Search-R1 and R-Search comparisons. Comparator membership within the fixed-opponent, verification, sampling and optimizer ablations also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 4 retain the same evaluation samples, pass@1 judging, retrieval configuration and training settings. Appendix A.3 newly identifies the RAG verifier for existing experiments without reporting a replacement or revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and Appendix B retain the same ablations and training-dynamics analyses. The trajectory examples and hacking cases in Appendices C and E also match. The added precision–recall discussion introduces no new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 6(c) already includes the same ±1 standard-deviation band in v2. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or revised uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: All benchmark, ablation, runtime and case-study results are retained. For example, Table 1's Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct +SSP average remains 49.5, and Table 6's GRPO–GRPO result remains 50.9 with 504.4 seconds per step. Plotted results also match.

T1.justification: The Markov-decision formulation, constrained self-play objective and equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. No mathematical definition, formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about proposer–solver co-evolution and performance improvements under from-scratch and continual training without additional human supervision. The contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly explains that verification prioritizes precision over recall and may reject valid questions. It argues that retaining high-confidence samples supports clean, stable training and co-evolution, adding a specific filtering limitation and mechanism interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly identifies Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct as the default RAG solver, motivated by sampling efficiency. v2 already named this model as the evaluation judge but lacked this explicit verifier-model disclosure. Other configurations, prompts and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged, including the positioning against task-synthesis and earlier LLM self-play approaches. The added ICLR publication notice does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 adds brief explanatory passages in Appendices A.3 and B.3 and updates title-page institutional and publication text. Section organization and the remaining prose are retained.

P2.justification: The title-page branding changes from Alibaba Qwen Applications Business Group to QWEN BUSINESS UNIT, and an ICLR 2026 publication footer is added. Appendix additions cause limited text reflow across pages 17–22; scientific figures, tables and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Identifying the RAG verifier in Appendix A.3 resolves a concrete implementation omission, while Appendix B.3 explicitly acknowledges valid-question rejection as a cost of precision-focused filtering. These provide a limited improvement in reproducibility and interpretation. The empirical evidence and main claims remain unchanged.
